provider.name: Canadensys
provider.organization_type: Canadian biodiversity data network, occurrence portal, publishing infrastructure, and standards community
provider.description: Canadensys is a Canadian biodiversity information network that supports publication, discovery, standardization, validation, georeferencing, and reuse of occurrence, specimen, collection, taxonomic, institutional, and dataset metadata.
institutional_context: Canadian natural history collections and biodiversity institutions
GBIF network and national biodiversity data publishing infrastructure
Integrated Publishing Toolkit deployments and Darwin Core standards

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting Canadensys documentation, occurrence and dataset metadata guidance, Darwin Core mappings, data publishing workflows, georeferencing and quality standards, APIs, licensing, citation instructions, and network context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: Canadensys and its publishing institutions remain authoritative for dataset metadata, occurrence records, publishing guidance, licenses, APIs, citation, legal terms, and contacts.

notes: Verify whether the data portal exposes a supported public API and whether paths differ from the seeds.
Do not infer undocumented endpoints from browser traffic alone.
Capture request parameters, pagination, filters, response schemas, download behavior, rate limits, examples, and legal conditions.
Distinguish portal APIs from IPT archives, GBIF APIs, and static downloads.
Capture exact dataset- and record-level license wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate occurrence metadata, media, sequence links, taxonomic content, and institutional descriptions.
Preserve publisher, rights holder, license URI, citation, dataset DOI, and source archive provenance.
Do not assume network-level openness overrides dataset-specific restrictions.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some paths, subdomains, or APIs may redirect, be renamed, be unavailable, or have moved to other infrastructure; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every occurrence record, taxon, dataset, institution, or IPT resource when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, publisher credentials, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Occurrence records, datasets, media, sequences, taxonomic content, and institutional metadata may carry different rights.
Always preserve dataset provenance, publisher attribution, license URI, archive version, and source identifiers.
